## DELETE `/api/instances/nasServer/name:{name}`

**Tier:** T3  

Delete a nasServer instance. This deletes the nasServer and its associated resources. Pre-requirements: Before deleting a NAS server, ensure that there are no file systems or VMware datastores associated with it. Otherwise an error will be returned.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | string | yes | User-specified name of the NAS server. |

_4 parameter(s) have no name in the source spec and are omitted._

**Request body** (required): `inline`

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `skipDomainUnjoin` | boolean | Indicates whether to keep the associated SMB servers joined to the Active Directory when the NAS server is deleted. Values are: true - Keep the associated SMB servers joined to the Active Directory when the NAS server… |
| `domainUsername` | string | Adminstrator login used to unjoin the associated SMB servers from the Active Directory (AD) domain before deleting the NAS server. This parameter is required when the skipDomainUnjoin parameter is false or not set, and… |
| `domainPassword` | string | Administrator password used to unjoin the associated SMB servers from the Active Directory (AD) domain before deleting the NAS server. This parameter is required when the skipDomainUnjoin parameter is false or not set,… |

**Responses:** `204` No Content

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `homeSP` | object | Specify the SP on which the VDM is to run. |
| `isReplicationDestination` | boolean | Specify whether the NAS server is a replication destination. Values are: true - Replication destination NAS server. false - Normal NAS server. |
| `isBackupOnly` | boolean | Specify whether the NAS server is used as backup only. Values are: true - NAS server acts as backup only. false - Normal NAS server. |
| `currentUnixDirectoryService` | `NasServerUnixDirectoryServiceEnum` | Define the Unix directory service used for looking up identity information for Unix such as UIDs, GIDs, net groups, and so on. \|Name\|Value\|Description\| \|----------\|----------\|----------\| \|None\|0\|No Unix… |
| `isMultiProtocolEnabled` | boolean | Indicates whether multiprotocol sharing mode is enabled. Values are: true - Enable multiprotocol sharing. false - Disable multiprotocol sharing. |
| `allowUnmappedUser` | boolean | Use this flag to mandatory disable access in case of any user mapping failure. Values are: true - Enable access in case of any user mapping failure. false - Disable access in case of any user mapping failure. |
| `defaultUnixUser` | string | Default Unix user name used for granting access in case of Windows to Unix user mapping failure. When empty, access in such case is denied. |
| `defaultWindowsUser` | string | Default Windows user name used for granting access in case of Unix to Windows user mapping failure. When empty, access in such case is denied. |
| `enableWindowsToUnixUsernameMapping` | boolean | Indicates whether a Unix to/from Windows user name mapping is enabled. Values are: true - Unix to/from Windows user name mapping is enabled. false - Unix to/from Windows user name mapping is disabled. |
| `isPacketReflectEnabled` | boolean |  |
| `isIgnoreWarnings` | boolean | Ignore warnings related to the operation. Values are: true - Ignore warnings. false(Default) - Warnings will interrupt the operation. |

**Responses:** `204` No Content
